9	
10	G003_guava = Google Guava core libraries (~610 java files in guava/src). Java 21 + Maven 3.9 present but **build needs network** (offline `./mvnw` fails: central-publishing-maven-plugin + all deps uncached in ~/.m2). So no full build/test — verify refactors by reading + standalone `javac` against hand-written stubs for external annotations (com.google.common.annotations.GwtCompatible, base.Function/Preconditions, errorprone.annotations.*, org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable).
11	
12	**Two flavors maintained in lock-step**: `guava/src/com/google/common/...` (JRE) and `android/guava/src/com/google/common/...` (Android). For escape package the files were byte-identical across flavors — apply same edit to both (cp jre→android). Also `guava-gwt/src-super/.../super/` holds GWT super-source twins, but ONLY for classes needing GWT-different emulation (e.g. escape/Platform.java has a GWT twin with non-ThreadLocal buffer). Don't put generic logic in Platform — it forces a needless GWT-twin edit.
13	
14	NOTE: most apparent duplication in Guava is INTENTIONAL — don't "fix" it. primitives/*Array expandedCapacity + */checkNoOverflow are pasted per-class on purpose (source comment "Unfortunately this is pasted from ImmutableCollection.Builder.") to avoid cross-package deps; Ascii.toUpper/toLowerCase + PercentEscaper UTF-8 branches + ArrayBased escaper fast-paths are deliberately inlined/unrolled for perf. Good targets = genuine missed dedups with a NATURAL home (shared superclass) or local cleanups that don't fight a design decision.
15	
16	REJECTED candidate (don't re-investigate): hash/`shiftMix(long val){return val ^ (val>>>47);}` is byte-identical in FarmHashFingerprint64 + Fingerprint2011 (both extend AbstractNonStreamingHashFunction, only 2 subclasses). DO NOT pull up — these are independent faithful C++ ports of Geoff Pike's algorithms (their K0/K1/K2 constants DIFFER), each inlines `x^=x>>>47` in some spots and uses shiftMix in others (local algorithm detail, not shared util), and AbstractNonStreamingHashFunction is a purpose-neutral structural base (Hasher plumbing, no algorithm constants) — injecting magic constant 47 there is wrong. Textbook intentional-independence. An Explore sweep for identical-helper-across-siblings-with-shared-superclass found this as the ONLY candidate in escape/math/base/hash/io/primitives/net/html/xml — i.e. the verifiable-package dedup well is essentially dry after refactors #1-#3. A SECOND sweep (dead private members + redundant-recompute-within-method, same packages) found NOTHING — code is exceptionally clean (e.g. Strings.commonSuffix repeated .length() is fine: O(1)+JIT-inlined). Also confirmed math/Stats+StatsAccumulator ALREADY consolidate their shared helper (calculateNewMeanNonFinite is one pkg-private static in StatsAccumulator, imported by Stats) — upstream had done that pair; #3 fixed the one they missed (PairedStats). Conclusion for future sessions: do NOT manufacture marginal/design-fighting edits here just to "keep going"; the high-confidence verifiable-refactor space is exhausted.
17	
18	**Refactor #3 (math pkg): consolidate duplicated ensurePositive/ensureInUnitRange.** PairedStats + PairedStatsAccumulator each had private static `ensurePositive` (identical) and `ensureInUnitRange` (PairedStats hand-rolled clamp; Accumulator used Doubles.constrainToRange — verified bit-exact equivalent incl NaN/±Inf/±0/subnormals). NOT intentional-independence dup (Accumulator already depends on PairedStats via snapshot(); PairedStats has no back-dep). Moved both helpers into PairedStats as package-private static, consolidated ensureInUnitRange on `Doubles.constrainToRange(value,-1,1)` (added Doubles import to PairedStats); Accumulator now calls `PairedStats.ensurePositive/ensureInUnitRange` and dropped its now-unused Doubles import. Home=PairedStats avoids a cycle (Accumulator→PairedStats already exists; reverse would cycle). Both @GwtIncompatible, no super-source twin. Net -46/+14 across 4 files (2 jre+2 android). Verified: standalone bit-exact test (22 edge cases) + 2-class same-package package-private static call reproduction. (Full math stub-compile is heavy — many deps — so verified the touched logic+mechanics standalone instead.)
19	
20	**Refactor #2 (escape pkg): ArrayBasedEscaperMap.createReplacementArray keySet()+get() → entrySet().** Removed redundant per-entry map.get() hash lookup; added `import java.util.Map.Entry;`. Matches sibling idiom (CharEscaperBuilder.toArray already uses entrySet). Behavior-identical (writes are key-indexed, order-independent). Applied to both flavors. Verified: full escape pkg stub-compiles clean + functional test (Escapers.builder→ArrayBasedCharEscaper, direct ArrayBasedUnicodeEscaper w/ escapeUnsafe, empty map, large keys, shared multi-entry map) all pass. Reusable stub harness lives at /tmp/esc (stubs for GwtCompatible/VisibleForTesting/Function/Preconditions/DoNotMock/CanIgnoreReturnValue/CheckReturnValue/Nullable/NullMarked); compile escape/*.java against `find /tmp/esc/stub -name '*.java'`.
21	
22	**Refactor #1 (escape pkg): pull up duplicated `growBuffer`.** `private static char[] growBuffer(char[],int,int)` was byte-for-byte identical in CharEscaper.java AND UnicodeEscaper.java (both extend `Escaper`). Moved it once into `Escaper` as package-private `static` (added `import static java.lang.System.arraycopy;` there); removed both private copies. Inherited static resolves unqualified from same-package subclasses. arraycopy static import stays in both subclasses (still used in escapeSlow). Verified: stub-compile EXIT=0 + functional test (long strings forcing buffer growth past 1024, surrogate pairs, char-strip, empty, no-escape fast path) all correct. -60/+34 lines across 6 files (3 jre + 3 android).
23

Done. I refactored the `com.google.common.escape` package to remove a clear, unintentional code duplication.

## What changed

The private helper `growBuffer(char[], int, int)` was **byte-for-byte identical** in both `CharEscaper` and `UnicodeEscaper`, which both extend the abstract `Escaper`. I pulled it up:

- **Added** to `Escaper` as a package-private `static` method (plus `import static java.lang.System.arraycopy`).
- **Removed** the two private copies from `CharEscaper` and `UnicodeEscaper`. Both subclasses still call it unqualified — it resolves to the inherited static — and both still import `arraycopy` for their own use elsewhere (`escapeSlow`), so no import broke.

Applied identically to both the **JRE flavor** (`guava/src/...`) and the **Android flavor** (`android/guava/src/...`), which were byte-identical and stay in lock-step. There's no GWT super-source twin for these three classes (only `Platform.java` has one), so nothing else needed touching.

Net: **−60 / +34 lines across 6 files**.

## Verification

The full project can't be built here (offline, deps uncached), so I verified the touched package directly:

- **Stub-compile** of both flavors against the annotation stubs → `EXIT=0`, all escape classes produced.
- **Functional test** exercising the actual `growBuffer` paths — buffer growth past 1024 chars for both a `CharEscaper` and an `ArrayBasedUnicodeEscaper` with surrogate pairs, plus empty-string and no-escape fast paths → **ALL PASS**.

This is a behavior-preserving deduplication: one canonical helper in the natural superclass home instead of two identical copies. I deliberately scoped it narrowly — most apparent duplication in Guava (per-class `expandedCapacity`, inlined UTF-8 branches, independent hash ports) is intentional and shouldn't be "fixed."

## What changed

The private helper `growBuffer(char[], int, int)` was **byte-for-byte identical** in both `CharEscaper` and `UnicodeEscaper`, which both extend the abstract `Escaper`. I pulled it up:

- **Added** to `Escaper` as a package-private `static` method (plus `import static java.lang.System.arraycopy`).
- **Removed** the two private copies from `CharEscaper` and `UnicodeEscaper`. Both subclasses still call it unqualified — it resolves to the inherited static — and both still import `arraycopy` for their own use elsewhere (`escapeSlow`), so no import broke.

Applied identically to both the **JRE flavor** (`guava/src/...`) and the **Android flavor** (`android/guava/src/...`), which were byte-identical and stay in lock-step. There's no GWT super-source twin for these three classes (only `Platform.java` has one), so nothing else needed touching.

Net: **−60 / +34 lines across 6 files**.

## Verification

The full project can't be built here (offline, deps uncached), so I verified the touched package directly:

- **Stub-compile** of both flavors against the annotation stubs → `EXIT=0`, all escape classes produced.
- **Functional test** exercising the actual `growBuffer` paths — buffer growth past 1024 chars for both a `CharEscaper` and an `ArrayBasedUnicodeEscaper` with surrogate pairs, plus empty-string and no-escape fast paths → **ALL PASS**.

This is a behavior-preserving deduplication: one canonical helper in the natural superclass home instead of two identical copies. I deliberately scoped it narrowly — most apparent duplication in Guava (per-class `expandedCapacity`, inlined UTF-8 branches, independent hash ports) is intentional and shouldn't be "fixed."
